name: Solitude-Vast
geological_features: Uniform cloud layers with minimal banding
A deep atmospheric vortex at the north pole
Metallic hydrogen core generating an immense magnetic field
specific_features: No moons, rings, or orbital companions of any kind
description: Solitude-Vast is a gas giant of unusual character, its atmosphere presenting uniform, muted cloud layers in shades of deep blue and grey that lack the dramatic banding typical of its class. A single polar vortex churns at the north pole, but otherwise the world's weather systems move with a slow, meditative cadence that seems almost deliberate in its restraint.

What makes Solitude-Vast truly remarkable is its absolute isolation. It possesses no moons, no rings, no trojans, no co-orbital companions of any kind. In a universe where gas giants typically accumulate retinues of captured bodies, this world drifts alone through its system, gravitationally pristine and utterly solitary.

The mechanism by which a planet of this mass has maintained its isolation defies current orbital mechanics models. Some theorists propose that its magnetic field, powered by a metallic hydrogen core of unusual density, creates an exclusion zone that deflects approaching bodies. Others suggest that something in the planet's formation history cleared its orbital neighborhood with unusual thoroughness.

Fuel-harvesting operations find Solitude-Vast ideal precisely because of its emptiness; there is no debris field to navigate, no moonlets to track, no ring system to avoid. The irony that the loneliest planet in the sector has become the busiest fueling station is not lost on the crews who work its atmosphere in rotating shifts, alone together above an empty giant.
